questions.question: In a MOS capacitor with p-type substrate, what charge carriers form the inversion layer?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Holes are the majority carriers in the bulk, not in inversion.
explanations.b: Correct. Electrons form the inversion layer in p-type material.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Ions are not mobile carriers in the semiconductor.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Protons are not involved in charge transport here.

questions.question: Which region is characterized by a widening depletion width but no inversion layer?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Flatband has no depletion region.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Accumulation has majority carriers at surface.
explanations.c: Correct. The depletion region expands with increasing gate voltage before inversion.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Inversion means the surface now has minority carriers.

questions.question: What happens to gate capacitance in inversion when measured at high frequency?

answers.b: It becomes constant at oxide capacitance

explanations.a: Incorrect. Inversion doesn't increase capacitance at high frequency.
explanations.b: Correct. Inversion charge can’t follow fast signals, so C ≈ C<sub>ox</sub>.
explanations.d: Incorrect. That's true only at low frequencies.

questions.question: Which of the following affects the flatband voltage?

explanations.a: Incorrect. It affects capacitance, not flatband voltage directly.
explanations.b: Correct. Flatband depends on the work function difference between gate and semiconductor.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Resistivity is not directly involved.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Permittivity affects electric field, not flatband.

questions.question: What is the ideal surface potential at threshold in a MOS capacitor?

explanations.c: Correct. At strong inversion, surface potential equals 2φ<sub>F</sub>.

questions.question: How does high-frequency behavior differ in MOS C-V characteristics?

answers.c: Inversion layer doesn’t respond, so capacitance stays low

explanations.a: Incorrect. High frequency suppresses inversion response.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Capacitance actually falls in depletion.
explanations.c: Correct. Minority carriers can't respond fast enough; capacitance remains near minimum.

questions.question: Which of these is a reason for threshold voltage shift in MOS capacitors?

explanations.a: Correct. Fixed oxide charges alter electric field, shifting V<sub>T</sub>.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Not relevant to threshold behavior.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Affects MOSFET scaling, not V<sub>T</sub> in a cap.
explanations.d: Incorrect. That’s a MOSFET behavior, not capacitor.

questions.question: In a MOS capacitor, increasing the substrate doping concentration will:

answers.c: Have no effect on threshold voltage

explanations.a: Incorrect. Higher doping requires more voltage to invert.
explanations.b: Correct. Higher doping increases 2φ<sub>F</sub> and charge needed for inversion, thus increasing V<sub>T</sub>.
explanations.c: Incorrect. V<sub>T</sub> is sensitive to substrate doping.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Depletion region always forms before inversion.

questions.question: What effect does a negative fixed charge in the oxide have on the MOS threshold voltage?

answers.d: It changes the substrate doping type

explanations.a: Incorrect. Negative charges attract positive charges in the semiconductor, reducing the V<sub>T</sub>.
explanations.b: Correct. Negative oxide charge aids inversion, reducing the threshold voltage.
explanations.c: Incorrect. It directly influences surface potential.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Doping type is not altered by oxide charges.
